content: Indian frankincense (Boswellia) should be dosed according to the specific indication. The recommended oral dosage is generally 300-500 mg taken twice or three times daily (BID/TID). For extracts, a common dosage is 333 mg taken three times daily (TID), or up to 3600 mg per day. Gum resin preparations are typically dosed at 350 mg TID or 300 mg TID orally. Higher doses may be required for conditions such as inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, asthma, diuretic purposes, or painful menstruation. Clinical trials have demonstrated beneficial effects of Boswellia for these conditions, but the consistency and reliability of the evidence vary. Adverse effects reported with Boswellia use include diarrhea and nausea, among others. During pregnancy, Boswellia may act as an emmenagogue (stimulating menstrual flow) and an abortifacient, and therefore it is categorized as avoid during pregnancy. There is no available data regarding its safety during lactation. However, in general, Boswellia is considered acceptable for use, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
